def-aov-oneway.title: The one-way layout
def-aov-oneway.html: A one-way layout has g≥2 groups with nk≥1 observations in group k and n=∑knk>g observations in all. Its cell-means form is 𝛍𝛆Ykj=μk+εkj,that is,Y=Zμ+ε, where Z is the n×g matrix whose column k is the indicator zk of group k and 𝛍μ=(μ1,…,μg)⊤. Its effects form is 𝛂𝛆Ykj=μ+αk+εkj,that is,Y=[1,Z](μα)+ε. In both, the errors have 𝛆E(ε)=0 and 𝛆Cov(ε)=σ2I. The normal one-way model adds 𝛆ε∼Nn(0,σ2I). The layout is balanced if n1=⋯=ng=m, say. The treatment parameters μk (or αk) are fixed effects: unknown constants attached to the g treatments actually studied.

eq-aov-M.html: M=∑k=1gzkzk⊤nk,(My)kj=y¯k,

eq-aov-hetero-bias.html: E(MSB)−E(MSE)=g(n−1)n(g−1)(n−g)∑k=1g(n¯−nk)σk2.

eq-aov-noncentrality.html: 𝛉γ=‖PTθ‖2σ2=1σ2∑k=1gnk(μk−μ¯)2,μ¯=1n∑k=1gnkμk.

eq-aov-pythagoras.html: ∑k,jykj2=ny¯2+∑knk(y¯k−y¯)2+∑k,j(ykj−y¯k)2.

eq-aov-sse.html: SSE=‖(I−M)y‖2=∑k=1g∑j=1nk(ykj−y¯k)2=∑k=1g(nk−1)sk2,

eq-aov-three-spaces.html: Rn=span(1)⏟dim⁡1⊕T⏟dim⁡g−1⊕C(Z)⊥⏟dim⁡n−g,I=P0+(M−P0)+(I−M),

eq-aov-weighted-orthogonality.html: ∑k=1gcikclknk=0(i≠l),

exm-aov-allocation.title: Forty observations in four groups
exm-aov-allocation.html: With n=40 and g=4, the guaranteed noncentrality per unit of (Δ/σ)2 is 5.000 for the balanced allocation 10,10,10,10, 3.938 for the mildly unbalanced 7,9,11,13, and 2.400 for 4,6,10,20. At Δ=σ the guaranteed powers of the level-0.05 test are 0.399, 0.320 and 0.205. To guarantee power 0.8, the range of the means must be at least 1.56σ, 1.76σ and 2.25σ respectively (Figure 15.5.1). The mild imbalance gives the same guarantee as a balanced design with 8×3.938≈31.5 observations, so it wastes a fifth of the experiment.

exm-aov-mortar.title: An unbalanced trial with unequal variances
exm-aov-mortar.title_html: An unbalanced trial with unequal variances
exm-aov-mortar.html:
A repair mortar was made with four admixture formulations, and its setting time was measured in minutes. The standard formulation A was tested most often, and the newer formulations least (simulated data, rounded to 0.1 minute):

Formulation nk Setting times (min) Mean sk
A 12 18.9, 20.2, 20.6, 21.2, 20.3, 19.0, 20.2, 19.0, 20.5, 20.6, 20.1, 20.3 20.075 0.73
B 9 22.6, 21.3, 22.2, 22.8, 19.3, 20.7, 21.5, 20.8, 18.8 21.111 1.38
C 6 20.7, 18.2, 18.6, 23.6, 21.3, 22.6 20.833 2.14
D 4 20.1, 22.6, 28.3, 25.3 24.075 3.53

The standard deviations grow as the group sizes shrink, the negative pairing of @exm-aov-size-simulation. The classical analysis gives F=5.34 on (3,27) degrees of freedom and p=0.0051, apparently strong evidence, driven by the high mean of D. But MSE=3.015 gives the variance of D weight 3/27, while the null expectation of MSB in @thm-aov-heteroscedastic(b) gives it weight (1−4/31)/3≈0.29; estimated with the sk2, that expectation is 5.407, far above MSE. Welch’s test gives FW=2.64 on (3, 8.3) degrees of freedom and p=0.119, and the Brown–Forsythe test gives FBF=2.98 on (3, 6.2) degrees of freedom and p=0.115. The difference between D and A is 4.00 minutes. With the pooled standard error 1.003 its 95% interval is [1.94, 6.06]; with the Welch–Satterthwaite standard error 1.776 on 3.1 degrees of freedom it is [−1.56, 9.56]. Four observations with a standard deviation of 3.5 minutes cannot establish a difference of four minutes.

The weighted and unweighted averages of the group means are 21.039 and 21.524, so the side conditions ∑knkαk=0 and ∑kαk=0 of Section 15.1 (@thm-est-side-conditions) define overall means that differ by half a minute here.

exm-aov-nitrogen-anova.title: The analysis of variance for the nitrogen trial
exm-aov-nitrogen-anova.title_html: The analysis of variance for the nitrogen trial
exm-aov-nitrogen-anova.html:
For the thirty yields of Section 15.1, with grand mean y¯=5.6930 t/ha:

Source df Sum of squares Mean square F
nitrogen rates 4 28.7074 7.1768 26.43
plots within rates 25 6.7887 0.2715
corrected total 29 35.4960

The mean row would add ny¯2=972.307 on one degree of freedom. The critical value is F0.05(4,25)=2.759, and the p-value is 1.2×10−8. The table says only that the treatment component of the mean is not zero; the contrasts of Section 15.2 and Section 15.4 say what it is. Since the data were simulated, the true noncentrality is known: γ=103.4, far more than needed for power near one.

exm-aov-nitrogen-planned.title: Two planned contrasts
exm-aov-nitrogen-planned.html:
The pooled standard deviation is s=0.5211 on 25 degrees of freedom. For ψ1, vc=16(1+4⋅116), the estimate is 2.110 t/ha with standard error 0.238, so t=8.87 and the 95% interval is [1.620, 2.600]. Fertilizer raises yield by roughly two tonnes per hectare. Its sum of squares is 21.370.

For ψ2 the estimate is 0.595 t/ha with standard error 0.301, t=1.98, two-sided p=0.059, and the interval [−0.025, 1.215]. The data are consistent with anything from no gain to a gain of more than a tonne: with six plots per rate, half a tonne is only about 1.7 standard errors of a pairwise difference.

exm-aov-nitrogen-trend.title: The shape of the nitrogen response
exm-aov-nitrogen-trend.title_html: The shape of the nitrogen response
exm-aov-nitrogen-trend.html:
The five rates are equally spaced and the design is balanced, so the integer contrasts above apply. The four single-degree-of-freedom sums of squares, each tested against s2=0.2715 on 25 degrees of freedom, are:

Component Sum of squares F p Share of SSB
linear 25.9121 95.42 5.1×10−10 90.3%
quadratic 2.7904 10.28 0.0037 9.7%
cubic 0.0049 0.02 0.89 0.0%
quartic 8.6×10−6 3.2×10−5 0.996 0.0%
rates (total) 28.7074 26.43

The pieces add to the between-rates sum of squares of @exm-aov-nitrogen-anova, and F is the average of the four single-degree-of-freedom F values. Yield rises with the rate and the rise flattens: the quadratic component is clearly significant. The cubic and quartic components together test whether a quadratic in the rate describes the five means; their sum of squares 0.0049 on two degrees of freedom gives F=0.009 and p=0.99 (Figure 15.4.1).

exm-aov-size-simulation.title: How far the level moves
exm-aov-size-simulation.html:
Four normal groups have equal means and standard deviations increasing geometrically from 1 to R. Three designs of 40 observations are compared: balanced (10 per group), positive pairing (sizes 4,6,10,20, the largest group most variable) and negative pairing (sizes 20,10,6,4, the smallest group most variable). For each design and each R, 40000 data sets were simulated and three level-0.05 tests applied: the classical F test and the tests of Welch and of Brown and Forsythe described below (Figure 15.5.2).

At R=3, @eq-aov-hetero-bias gives expected mean square ratios E(MSB)/E(MSE) of 1.000, 0.559 and 1.923 for the three designs. The simulated levels of the classical test follow: 0.071 when balanced, 0.011 with positive pairing, and 0.241 with negative pairing, almost five times the nominal level. At R=4 the negative pairing gives 0.288. Welch’s test stays between 0.048 and 0.068 throughout, and the Brown–Forsythe test between 0.048 and 0.065.

The simulation supports the common rule of thumb that a ratio of about two between the largest and smallest standard deviations does little harm, but only with balance: at R=2 the balanced level is 0.059, while the two unbalanced designs give 0.015 and 0.160.

exr-aov-all-bases.title: C1
exr-aov-all-bases.html: Let U=[u1,…,ug−1] and V=[v1,…,vg−1] be two orthonormal bases of the treatment space. Show that V=UQ for an orthogonal (g−1)×(g−1) matrix Q, that the vectors of squared coordinates of y in the two bases have the same sum SSB, and that the individual squared coordinates generally differ. More generally, show that for any symmetric idempotent A of rank q and 𝛉Y∼Nn(θ,σ2I), Y⊤AY splits into q independent scaled noncentral χ2(1) variables, one for each vector of an orthonormal basis of C(A).

exr-aov-all-contrasts-zero.title: A2
exr-aov-all-contrasts-zero.html: Show that μ1=⋯=μg iff ∑kckμk=0 for every contrast c (∑kck=0), and iff μk−μg=0 for k=1,…,g−1.

exr-aov-averaging-group.title: C1
exr-aov-averaging-group.html: Let G be the set of n×n permutation matrices that permute observations only within groups. Show that M=1|G|∑Π∈GΠ, so the one-way projection is the average over the symmetries of the design. Deduce that C(Z) is exactly the set of vectors fixed by every Π∈G.

exr-aov-balanced-contrast-power.title: B1
exr-aov-balanced-contrast-power.html: In a balanced layout with m observations per group, show that the noncentrality of the test of a contrast is δ2=mψ2/(σ2∑kck2). How many observations per group are needed for the test of μ5−μ3 in the nitrogen trial to have power 0.8 at level 0.05 when the true difference is 0.5 t/ha and σ=0.5? (Use software for the noncentral F, or the normal approximation.)

exr-aov-bf-two.title: B2
exr-aov-bf-two.html: Show that for g=2 the Brown–Forsythe statistic also equals tW2, and that its degrees of freedom f equal νW. So the two robust tests coincide for two groups and differ only for three or more.

exr-aov-computing-formula.title: A2
exr-aov-computing-formula.html: Show from @eq-aov-pythagoras that SSB=∑kTk2/nk−T2/n and SSE=∑k,jykj2−∑kTk2/nk.

exr-aov-contrast-allocation.title: B2
exr-aov-contrast-allocation.html: A single contrast c matters above all. For a fixed total n, show that vc=∑kck2/nk is minimized, over positive real nk with ∑knk=n, by nk∝|ck|, with minimum (∑k|ck|)2/n. What does this say about how to allocate plots between two treatments, and between a control and the average of four treatments?

exr-aov-contrast-family-rank.title: C2
exr-aov-contrast-family-rank.html: The Scheffé multiplier for a family of contrasts depends on the dimension of the space the family spans (@thm-mc-scheffe). Show that the g−1 comparisons with a control span T, and that the family of the four “successive differences” μk+1−μk does too. Why, then, are Bonferroni or Dunnett intervals shorter than Scheffé’s for these families?

exr-aov-contrast-hetero.title: C2
exr-aov-contrast-hetero.html: In a balanced layout with variances σk2, show that the pooled variance estimate of the pairwise difference Y¯k−Y¯l, 2s2/m, has expectation 2σ¯2/m with σ¯2=g−1∑iσi2, while the true variance is (σk2+σl2)/m. Conclude that balance protects the overall test but not individual comparisons, and find the ratio of true to estimated variance for the two most variable groups when the variances are 1,2,4,8.

exr-aov-contrast-scale.title: A2
exr-aov-contrast-scale.html: Show directly that the t statistic of @prp-aov-contrast-ss(b) with ψ0=0 is unchanged when c is multiplied by a>0 and changes sign when a<0. What happens to the confidence interval?

exr-aov-contrast-se.title: A1
exr-aov-contrast-se.html: In the nitrogen trial, compute by hand the estimate and standard error of 12(μ4+μ5)−12(μ1+μ2), the average of the two highest rates minus the average of the two lowest, from the rate means of Section 15.1 and s=0.5211.

exr-aov-contrast-within-f.title: B3
exr-aov-contrast-within-f.html: In the nitrogen trial, compute the Scheffé-maximal contrast ck=nk(y¯k−y¯) from the rate means, and verify that its squared t statistic is 4F. Describe in words what it compares.

exr-aov-dunnett-correlation.title: B4
exr-aov-dunnett-correlation.html: With n0 observations on the control and nt on each treatment, show that the estimates Y¯k−Y¯0 and Y¯l−Y¯0 of two treatment-versus-control differences have correlation nt/(nt+n0). In a balanced design it is 12.

exr-aov-eta2-null.title: B2
exr-aov-eta2-null.html: In the normal model with equal means E(η2)=(g−1)/(n−1), which is not zero, so η2 overstates the treatment variation in small experiments. Show that the numerator of ω^2=SSB−(g−1)MSESSB+SSE has expectation ∑knk(μk−μ¯)2, whatever the means, so that it removes the bias from the numerator. When is ω^2 negative?

exr-aov-extend-planned.title: B1
exr-aov-extend-planned.html: Show that the two planned contrasts of @exm-aov-nitrogen-planned, (−1,14,14,14,14) and (0,0,−1,0,1), are orthogonal. Find two further contrasts that complete them to a complete orthogonal set, and say what they compare.

exr-aov-factorial-contrasts.title: A2
exr-aov-factorial-contrasts.html: For the four fertilizer combinations of “Factorial treatments”, verify that the three contrasts are orthogonal when every group has the same size, and that the P and K contrasts are not orthogonal for group sizes 3,3,3,5 (in the order none, P, K, both). What does the lack of orthogonality mean for the estimates?

exr-aov-fill-table.title: A1
exr-aov-fill-table.html: A one-way experiment with four treatments and six observations per treatment gives a treatment mean square of 12.0 and a corrected total sum of squares of 96.0. Complete the analysis of variance table, compute F and η2, and state the reference distribution of F under equal means.

exr-aov-guarantee-thirty.title: B4
exr-aov-guarantee-thirty.html: For n=30 observations in five groups, compare the quantity h of @prp-aov-balance-power for the balanced allocation and for the allocation 10,5,5,5,5 suggested by @exr-aov-sqrt-rule for comparisons with a control. What does each allocation optimize?

exr-aov-hetero-balanced.title: A1
exr-aov-hetero-balanced.html: For the balanced design with m=10 and variances 1,2,4,8, compute E(MSB) under equal means and E(MSE) from @thm-aov-heteroscedastic. Repeat for the sizes 4,6,10,20 and for 20,10,6,4.

exr-aov-intraclass.title: C1
exr-aov-intraclass.html: In a balanced layout, suppose that under equal means the errors within a group are equicorrelated, Cov(εkj,εkj′)=ρσ2 for j≠j′ with ρ≥0, and independent between groups. Show that E(MSE)=σ2(1−ρ) and E(MSB)=σ2(1−ρ+mρ). What happens to the level of the F test with m=10 and ρ=0.1?

exr-aov-invariance.title: C2
exr-aov-invariance.html: Show that F is unchanged when y is replaced by ay+b1 with a≠0, and when the observations are permuted within groups. Show that it changes when a constant is added to the observations of one group only, and explain why it should.

exr-aov-leverage.title: A2
exr-aov-leverage.html: Show that the hat matrix of the one-way model has diagonal entries 1/nk and that Var(ekj)=σ2(1−1/nk). What is the residual of an observation that is alone in its group, and why is it useless for checking the model?

exr-aov-poly5-check.title: A1
exr-aov-poly5-check.html: Check that the four polynomial contrasts for five levels are pairwise orthogonal. Show that the quadratic contrast vanishes when μk=a+bk, and the cubic contrast vanishes when μk=a+bk+ck2.

exr-aov-random-direction.title: C1
exr-aov-random-direction.html: Let q=g−1≥2 and let u be uniformly distributed on the unit sphere of the q-dimensional space T (for example u=w/‖w‖ with w∼N on T with covariance PT). Show that Ecos2⁡φ=1/q, where φ is the angle between u and a fixed nonzero v∈T. Interpret this with @prp-aov-contrast-angle.

exr-aov-random-effects-mean.title: C2
exr-aov-random-effects-mean.html: In the random-effects model of “Fixed and random effects”, show that Var(Y¯)=σ2/n+σa2∑knk2/n2. For fixed n and g, which group sizes make the grand mean most precise? Contrast this with the fixed-effects model, where Var(Y¯)=σ2/n whatever the group sizes.

exr-aov-random-n0.title: C1
exr-aov-random-n0.html: In the random-effects model Cov(Y)=σ2I+σa2ZZ⊤, E(Y)=μ1, use @thm-rv-quadform-mean to show that E(SSB)=(g−1)σ2+(n−∑knk2/n)σa2 and E(SSE)=(n−g)σ2. Show that n0=(n−∑knk2/n)/(g−1)≤n/g, with equality iff the layout is balanced.

exr-aov-randomization-mean.title: B3
exr-aov-randomization-mean.html: In the setting of “Where the model comes from”, suppose N units with values u1,…,uN are divided at random into groups of fixed sizes n1,…,ng, and unit i in group k yields ui+τk. Show that E(Y¯k)=τk+u¯ and that Cov(Ykj,Yk′j′)=−Su2/N for two different units, where Su2=∑i(ui−u¯)2/(N−1). Hint: the sum of the N deviations ui−u¯ is zero.

exr-aov-side-conditions.title: B1
exr-aov-side-conditions.html: Derive the three rows of the table in “What the parameters mean”. Then show that under ∑knkαk=0 the least squares estimates are μ^=y¯ and α^k=y¯k−y¯, and that ∑knkα^k2=∑knk(y¯k−y¯)2.

exr-aov-small-layout.title: A1
exr-aov-small-layout.html: For a one-way layout with group sizes 2,1,3, write down Z, M and I−M with the observations listed group by group. What is the residual of the observation in group 2, and why? How many degrees of freedom does the error space have, and which groups contribute to them?

exr-aov-sqrt-rule.title: B3
exr-aov-sqrt-rule.html: In a comparison of g−1 treatments with a control, suppose the control gets n0 observations and each treatment gets nt, with n0+(g−1)nt=n fixed. Show that ∑kVar(Y¯k−Y¯0) is minimized when n0=g−1nt. For g=5 and n=30, what allocation does this suggest?

exr-aov-symmetric-sizes.title: B3
exr-aov-symmetric-sizes.html: Four equally spaced levels have group sizes 2,4,4,2. Show that the classical linear contrast (−3,−1,1,3) is orthogonal for this design to the quadratic (1,−1,−1,1) but not to the cubic (−1,3,−3,1). Explain the first fact by symmetry.

exr-aov-tree-nitrogen.title: B4
exr-aov-tree-nitrogen.html: Use the formula of @prp-aov-tree-contrasts to recompute the sum of squares of the control against the fertilized rates in the nitrogen trial from the rate means, and compare it with the value 21.3701 in the text.

exr-aov-trend-lof.title: C2
exr-aov-trend-lof.html: For g equally spaced levels with equal group sizes, show that the sum of the sums of squares of the polynomial contrasts of degrees d+1,…,g−1 is the lack-of-fit sum of squares of the polynomial regression of degree d<g−1 on the level score, and that the sum for degrees 1,…,d is that regression’s sum of squares after the mean.

exr-aov-two-group-power.title: B1
exr-aov-two-group-power.html: For g=2 with n1+n2=n fixed, show that γ=(μ1−μ2)2n1n2/(nσ2), and that it is largest for n1=n2. By how much does the noncentrality fall for the split n1=n/4, n2=3n/4?

exr-aov-two-groups.title: B2
exr-aov-two-groups.html: For g=2, show that the pooled variance of the one-way model is the pooled variance of the two-sample t test, and that the t statistic for μ1−μ2 is (y¯1−y¯2)/(s1/n1+1/n2). (Section 15.3 shows that its square is the one-way F statistic.)

exr-aov-unequal-spacing.title: B2
exr-aov-unequal-spacing.html: Five plots at each of four rates 0, 1, 2 and 4 (in units of 50 kg N/ha) are to be analysed for trend. Show that the linear and quadratic orthogonal polynomial contrasts are proportional to (−7,−3,1,9) and (7,−4,−8,5). Check that the quadratic contrast vanishes when the means are linear in the rate.

exr-aov-welch-contrast.title: B3
exr-aov-welch-contrast.html: Let V^=∑kck2sk2/nk with independent sk2∼σk2χ2(nk−1)/(nk−1) under normality. Show that EV^=V=Var(ψ^) and VarV^=2∑k(ck2σk2/nk)2/(nk−1). Choose ν so that νV^/V has the mean and variance of a χ2(ν) variable, and show that replacing σk2 by sk2 in the answer gives the degrees of freedom of the Welch–Satterthwaite interval.

exr-aov-welch-two.title: B1
exr-aov-welch-two.html: Show that for g=2 the Welch statistic FW equals tW2, where tW=(y¯1−y¯2)/s12/n1+s22/n2, and that νW is Satterthwaite’s (s12/n1+s22/n2)2/[(s12/n1)2/(n1−1)+(s22/n2)2/(n2−1)].

prp-aov-balance-power.title: Balance maximizes the guaranteed noncentrality
prp-aov-balance-power.html:
In a one-way layout with group sizes n1,…,ng, g≥2, let h=mink≠lnknlnk+nl=mink≠l(1nk+1nl)−1.

  1. For all means with maxkμk−minkμk≥Δ>0, the noncentrality of the F test satisfies γ≥hΔ2/σ2, and there is a configuration with range exactly Δ at which equality holds.

  2. For fixed n=∑knk, h≤n/(2g), with equality iff the layout is balanced.

prp-aov-contrast-angle.title: The noncentrality of a contrast
prp-aov-contrast-angle.html: Let c be a contrast with vector uc∈T, and suppose 𝛉PTθ≠0. The noncentrality of the test of ψ=0 in @prp-aov-contrast-ss is δ2=ψ2σ2vc=γTcos2⁡φ, where φ is the angle between uc and 𝛉PTθ. In particular δ2≤γT, with equality iff uc is parallel to 𝛉PTθ, that is, iff ck∝nk(μk−μ¯).

prp-aov-contrast-ss.title: Sum of squares and test for a contrast
prp-aov-contrast-ss.title_html: Sum of squares and test for a contrast
prp-aov-contrast-ss.html:
In the normal one-way model, let ψ=∑kckμk be a contrast, ψ^=∑kckY¯k, and ψ0∈R. Then:

  1. ψ^∼N(ψ,σ2vc), and ψ^ is independent of s2;

  2. the statistic T=ψ^−ψ0svc∼t(n−g,δ),δ=ψ−ψ0σvc, so the test of ψ=ψ0 rejects when |T|>tn−g,α/2, and ψ^±tn−g,α/2svc is an exact 1−α confidence interval for ψ;

  3. the sum of squares of the contrast SS(c)=ψ^2vc=‖PcY‖2, where Pc projects onto the line spanned by uc, has one degree of freedom, and SS(c)/s2=T2 for ψ0=0 has the F(1,n−g,δ2) distribution. Replacing c by ac with a≠0 changes neither SS(c) nor the test;

  4. SS(c)≤∑knk(Y¯k−Y¯)2, with equality when ck=nk(Y¯k−Y¯) for every k.

prp-aov-tree-contrasts.title: Contrasts from successive splits
prp-aov-tree-contrasts.html:
For a set S of levels split into disjoint nonempty parts A and B, let NA=∑k∈Ank and NB=∑k∈Bnk, and define the contrast ck(S)={nk/NA,k∈A,−nk/NB,k∈B,0,k∉S. Its estimate is y¯A−y¯B, the difference between the means of all observations in A and in B, and SS(c(S))=NANBNA+NB(y¯A−y¯B)2.

  1. Every contrast d that is zero outside A (or outside B) is orthogonal to c(S) for the design.

  2. Split the set of all g levels into two parts, split each part with more than one level into two, and continue until every part is a single level. The g−1 contrasts of the splits form a complete set of orthogonal contrasts, whatever the group sizes.

thm-aov-heteroscedastic.title: Expected mean squares under unequal variances
thm-aov-heteroscedastic.title_html: Expected mean squares under unequal variances
thm-aov-heteroscedastic.html:
Let the Ykj be uncorrelated with E(Ykj)=μk and Var(Ykj)=σk2, and write n¯=n/g. Then:

  1. E(SSE)=∑k(nk−1)σk2, so E(MSE) is the average of the σk2 weighted by nk−1;

  2. E(SSB)=∑k(1−nk/n)σk2+∑knk(μk−μ¯)2;

  3. when the means are equal, E(MSB)−E(MSE)=g(n−1)n(g−1)(n−g)∑k=1g(n¯−nk)σk2.{#eq-aov-hetero-bias}

    In a balanced layout this is zero, and both mean squares estimate g−1∑kσk2. In an unbalanced layout it is positive when the larger variances belong to the smaller groups and negative when they belong to the larger groups.

thm-aov-oneway-ems.title: Expected mean squares in the one-way layout
thm-aov-oneway-ems.title_html: Expected mean squares in the one-way layout
thm-aov-oneway-ems.html:
In the one-way model of @def-aov-oneway (uncorrelated errors with common variance σ2, not necessarily normal):

  1. E(MSE)=σ2;

  2. E(MSB)=σ2+1g−1∑k=1gnk(μk−μ¯)2;

  3. in the effects form, ∑knk(μk−μ¯)2=∑knk(αk−α¯)2 with α¯=n−1∑knkαk, which is ∑knkαk2 under the side condition ∑knkαk=0. In a balanced layout it is m∑k(μk−μ~)2 with μ~=g−1∑kμk, which is m∑kαk2 under ∑kαk=0;

  4. E(MSB)≥E(MSE), with equality iff μ1=⋯=μg.

thm-aov-oneway-f.title: The one-way F test
thm-aov-oneway-f.title_html: The one-way F test
thm-aov-oneway-f.html:
In the normal one-way model of @def-aov-oneway, with mean vector 𝛉𝛍θ=Zμ, put MSB=SSBg−1,s2=MSE=SSEn−g,F=MSBMSE.

  1. Y¯, SSB=∑knk(Y¯k−Y¯)2 and SSE=∑k,j(Ykj−Y¯k)2 are mutually independent.

  2. SSE/σ2∼χ2(n−g), and SSB/σ2∼χ2(g−1,γ) with 𝛉γ=‖PTθ‖2σ2=1σ2∑k=1gnk(μk−μ¯)2,μ¯=1n∑k=1gnkμk.{#eq-aov-noncentrality}

  3. F∼F(g−1,n−g,γ), and γ=0 iff μ1=⋯=μg. In particular, when the means are equal, F∼F(g−1,n−g) whatever their common value and σ2.

  4. F is the statistic of the F test of the reduced model E(Y)∈span(1) against C(Z), and of the testable hypothesis α1=⋯=αg in the effects form. The test that rejects when F>Fα(g−1,n−g) is the likelihood ratio test of equal means. Its power is a continuous, strictly increasing function of γ, equal to α at γ=0.

thm-aov-orthogonal-contrasts.title: Orthogonal contrasts decompose the treatment sum of squares
thm-aov-orthogonal-contrasts.title_html: Orthogonal contrasts decompose the treatment sum of squares
thm-aov-orthogonal-contrasts.html:
In the one-way model, let c1,…,cg−1 be contrasts that are pairwise orthogonal for the design, ∑k=1gcikclknk=0(i≠l),{#eq-aov-weighted-orthogonality}

and write ψi=∑kcikμk and Fi=SS(ci)/s2.

  1. The vectors uc1,…,ucg−1 form an orthogonal basis of the treatment space T, and SSB=∑i=1g−1SS(ci).

  2. In the normal one-way model, SS(c1),…,SS(cg−1) and SSE are mutually independent, and SS(ci)/σ2∼χ2(1,γi) with γi=ψi2/(σ2vci). The noncentralities add up to that of the F test: ∑iγi=γ of @eq-aov-noncentrality.

  3. The F statistic is the average of the single-degree-of-freedom statistics: F=(g−1)−1∑iFi.

  4. In a balanced layout, @eq-aov-weighted-orthogonality reduces to ∑kcikclk=0.

  5. Conversely, every orthogonal basis u1,…,ug−1 of T arises in this way: if ui takes the value vik on group k, then cik=nkvik defines a complete set of orthogonal contrasts with uci=ui.
